newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: HEALTH FUNDS WELCOME PROPOSED CHANGES
Radical reforms have been recommended for the private health insurance industry.
The proposals are contained in a draft report by the Productivity Commission commissioned by the Federal Government after criticism of premium rises.
The report's been welcomed by the industry, which says the reforms would allow funds to charge less and offer more choice.
Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, has ruled out changes which would allow funds to charge older people higher premiums.
But Dr Wooldridge has appeared to welcome recommendations which would reward long-term fund members through no-claim bonuses and better benefits.
Other recommendations include penalties for those who wait to take up insurance, and allowing funds to choose which private hospitals they deal with.
The industry says the changes would reward loyal members, help the industry offer cheaper, tailor-made packages, and help the industry ensure hospitals perform well.
DOUBLE-MURDER SUICIDE IN MELBOURNE
In Melbourne, Homicide Squad detectives say a man stabbed to death a 9 year-old girl and a 7 year-old boy at suburban Deer Park last night, before throwing himself under a truck.
They're treating the deaths as a double murder-suicide.
Police say the children had their throats cut with a kitchen knife, in their Wakool Avenue house, between nine thirty and ten last night.
Detective Sergeant Gavan Ryan says the children were being cared for by the man, while his wife was playing bingo with relatives.
The man's two children, aged 4 years and 18 months, who were in the house at the time, were not injured.
SOURCE OF HOSPITAL SALMONELLA OUTBREAK STILL A MYSTERY
All bar four of the 27 people affected by an outbreak of salmonella poisoning at Brisbane's Mater Hospital have now gone home.

A 92-year-old woman has died from salmonella poisoning after being admitted to the hospital for an unrelated procedure. Another three remain in the hospital, but their conditions haven't been released.
Most of the cases were confined to patients in the Mater Mothers, and training staff.
The hospital is refusing to say whether action's been taken against the Mater since the death of the woman.
The source of the outbreak hasn't yet been identified.
NSW SAYS NO TO INTEGRATED IR SYSTEM
New South Wales has refused to co-operate with moves by the Federal Government for a single industrial relations system in Australia.
Industrial Relations Ministers met in Melbourne yesterday to discuss the Commonwealth's proposal for uniform legislation.
But New South Wales Labour Minister, Jeff Shaw, says he'll only agree to uniform unfair dismissal laws if they're similar to his state's.
Mr Shaw says New South Wales wants to maintain the integrity of its own system.
He says the Carr Government doesn't want to be fused with the federal laws, and to assist those laws to override the good workplace agreements he says are being put in place in New South Wales.
COMPLAINTS OVER MEDIA COVERAGE IN PORT LINCOLN
The Mayor of Port Lincoln in South Australia, has complained to the Press Council with claims recent coverage of his comments about race are irresponsible, outragous, and inflamatory.
Peter Davis has also written to the Race Discrimination Commission about the coverage, which is being blamed for a racial slur on the city.
Mayor Davis, who described children of mixed-race as mongrels, has apologised for his comments, but intends to continue speaking out against multiculturism.
The comments saw the resignation of nine of the ten councillors, a by-election, and a new look Council made up of a majority of Davis supporters.
The only Councillor not to resign, Mick Baskin has also condemned the media's actions.
BOY FOUND DROWNED ON PROPERTY
A three year-old boy from Barellan in the Riverina district of New South Wales drowned yesterday after wandering off his parents' property.
Police say the boy had been playing with a younger child when the three year-old's mother noticed them both missing just after two o'clock.
The boy's body was found a short time later when police searched a nearby dam.
A post-mortem examination will be held in Sydney this morning, police say the other child was found safe and well.
NSW BLOOD BANK LOOKING FOR CHRISTMAS DONORS
The Red Cross Blood bank is calling on New South Wales donors to increase its supplies for the Christmas/New Year period.
The blood bank's Carol O'Shea says supplies are well down on last year and there are just four collection days before Christmas, traditionally a period of heavy demand.
Ms O'Shea says all blood types are needed, but groups O and A are the two most common, and the two the blood bank anticipates will be in greatest demand.
Ms O'Shea says the blood bank is always looking for O-negative donors because it's the one blood type that in an emergency may be transferred to any blood group.
DEMOCRATS WEIGH INTO MOBILE PHONE TOWER DEBATE
The Australian Democrats are calling for local councils to have the power to choose sites for mobile phone towers.
This follows more than 40 arrests of protestors in the central Victorian town of Daylesford this week.
The residents are protesting at construction of a Telstra tower, saying they're worried about its radiation levels.
Telstra remains undeterred, but Democrats Communications spokeswoman Senator Lynn Allison, wants the Federal Government to change the law so councils can approve or reject tower sites. - - - -
CRICKET: MOODY STARS IN WARRIORS WIN
In cricket, Western Australia came through in a surprise victory over South Australia in the day-night match at the WACA last night.
Some flashy fielding saw W-A dismiss the Redbacks for 171 in 47 overs.
Western Australia was struggling earlier in the game but a match saving 101 not out from captain Tom Moody put the side in with a chance, finishing on nine for 210 after 50 overs.
